Definition: from G1537 and a derivative of G739; to finish out (time); figuratively, to equip fully (a teacher):--accomplish, thoroughly furnish.
BiblicalUsage: exartízō means accomplish, thoroughly furnish. In Acts 21:5, the text says "And when we had accomplished those days."
TheologicalSignificance: In exartízō I find no hidden theology; it simply means accomplish, thoroughly furnish.
